utterance: `inspection-vpc` (10.70.0.0/16) is the inspection workload's network, and `10.70.1.0/24` and `10.70.2.0/24` are its appliance-tier subnets — the space anything inspecting the workload's traffic sits in. Nothing in the network is load-balanced yet: it holds no load balancer, no target group and no instance of any kind. Stand up the front of the inspection fleet: launch one t2.micro appliance into `10.70.1.0/24`, put a Gateway Load Balancer across both appliance-tier subnets in front of it, and give that load balancer a listener whose only default action forwards to an instance-type target group in `inspection-vpc` on GENEVE port 6081 carrying that appliance registered on port 6081.

main.responsibility: owns the application's resources and their configuration
main.intent: inspection-vpc runs one new t2.micro appliance of the agent's own, standing in the segment the account marks as the place the workload's appliances land; the workload's inspected traffic goes through one gateway load balancer spanning exactly the segments of inspection-vpc that are the workload's appliance tier and in service when the work ends — the front the account already keeps for that traffic, when it keeps one — carrying a listener whose single default action forwards to an instance-type GENEVE:6081 target group in inspection-vpc, the group the account already keeps for that purpose when it keeps one, whose registered targets on port 6081 are exactly that appliance
